benchmarks.task_description:
fix(system-ship): a restart keeps a repo's open questions for the answer

Fixes #957

## Problem
A held repo reaches the user only when the run escalates as a whole (AC-186.3). The user then answers by starting `/system:ship <spec>` again. While the run is escalated, `repo resume` refuses with "resume it with /system:ship". `system ship start` then set every escalated repo back to `ready` and dropped `questions`, so `repo resume --answer` was refused with "is ready, not escalated" and the repo rebuilt from scratch without the answer. Journey 25 went round this three times, at about 19 min and 2–3 M tokens.

## Change
- `appship_state.start`: a repo escalated **with questions** stays escalated with them, and only `held` is cleared. `next` then returns `answer` for it and `repo resume <id> --answer` takes the user's answer (AC-186.2). A repo escalated without questions (cause code, environment or platform) restarts as before, as in AC-097.4.
- `plugins/system/commands/ship.md`, `action: answer`: resume with the user's answer as well as with suggested answers. The rule entry R14 quotes the new sentence, and the file does not grow (333 bytes before and after). System plugin 1.24.3.

## Tests
`tests/cplat/test_ship_restart_keeps_questions_957.py` (restart keeps the questions, `next` asks `answer`, resume works; a repo without questions restarts). The spec 097, 155 and 186 suites pass, as do the rules check and the full selected suite (one AC-180.4 timeout under load passed on rerun).

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(security): name the target in confirmation dialogs

## Why

Follow-up to #67. `_message` in `src/beaconmcp/confirm.py` has a dedicated sentence for the BMC, snapshot, restore and self-update tools, and falls back to `Run {tool}?` for everything else. That fallback is what the user gets for `proxmox_vm_create` and `proxmox_vm_config` (both in `DEFAULT_CONFIRM_TOOLS` since #67), and for `ssh_run` / `proxmox_run` when an operator lists them in `server.confirm_tools`. So the dialog that is supposed to be the human check shows neither the node, nor the guest, nor the key that tripped the rule, nor the command. Approving it is approving blind.

## Changes

- `proxmox_vm_create`: `Create lxc 120 on pve1? Sensitive settings: hookscript, mp0=local:102/vm-102-disk-9.raw,mp=/mnt.`
- `proxmox_vm_config`: `Change the config of VM 7 on pve1? Sensitive settings: hostpci0.`
- `ssh_run`: `Run on web1: <command>`, `proxmox_run`: `Run in guest 101 on pve1: <command>` -- command on one line, control characters stripped, line breaks rendered as ` ⏎ `; over 200 chars it is cut in the middle, keeps both ends and says how many chars are hidden
- `_sensitive_keys(cfg)` returns the keys that trip the rule; `_sensitive_config` is now `bool(_sensitive_keys(cfg))`. Same branches, same order, rule unchanged
- values are shown only for `rootfs` and the disk keys (same middle cut at 80), where the value *is* the thing to review; other keys are named without their value so `cipassword` and friends never reach the dialog
- unknown tools keep `Run {tool}?`

## Known and left alone

- `confirm_destructive` is untouched.
- A disk value is shown as given. If someone puts a secret in a volume path it would show; I don't think that is a real case.
- The command stays on one dialog line (no fake second line); its line breaks show as ` ⏎ `. The middle of a long script is hidden, with the count of hidden chars.
- Invisible and bidi Unicode characters and C1 controls are not filtered.
- The dashboard chat card has its own rendering (#64) and is not changed here.

## Related

#64, #67.

## Tests

1006 passed, ruff clean, Python 3.12.

     confirm: bool = Field(default=False, description="Yes, do it")
 
 
+_LINE_BREAK = " ⏎ "
+
+
+def _flat(text: Any) -> str:
+    """One line, no control characters, runs of whitespace collapsed."""
+    return " ".join(re.sub(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f]", " ", str(text)).split())
+
+
+def _clip(text: str, limit: int) -> str:
+    """Cap at ``limit`` characters, keeping both ends.
+
+    The cut is in the middle and says how much it hides, so that neither a
+    padded start nor a padded end can push the rest out of the dialog unseen.
+    """
+    if len(text) <= limit:
+        return text
+    head = limit * 3 // 5
+    tail = limit - head
+    return f"{text[:head]} [... {len(text) - limit} chars not shown ...] {text[-tail:]}"
+
+
+def _command(text: Any, limit: int = 200) -> str:
+    """A shell command on one dialog line, with its line breaks left visible.
+
+    A newline separates two commands for the shell, so it is rendered as a
+    mark instead of a space: ``echo a`` + newline + ``rm -rf /srv`` must not
+    read as a single echo.
+    """
+    lines = re.split(r"\r\n|\r|\n", str(text).strip())
+    # the second split drops the double space an empty line leaves behind
+    return _clip(" ".join(_LINE_BREAK.join(_flat(line) for line in lines).split()), limit)
+
+
+def _flagged(cfg: Any) -> str:
+    """Sensitive config keys for a dialog. Only disk and mount values are shown
+    (clipped); other values may hold secrets such as cipassword."""
+    if not isinstance(cfg, dict):
+        return ""
+    by_key = {str(k).strip().lower(): v for k, v in cfg.items()}
+    return ", ".join(
+        f"{k}={_clip(_flat(by_key[k]), 80)}" if k == "rootfs" or _DISK_KEY.match(k) else k

+    )

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(ssh): expire cached connections on idle, one per host

## Why

Two things in the SSH connection cache (`src/beaconmcp/ssh/client.py`, `_get_connection`), both from reading `main` at 861748a.

The TTL is counted from `created_at`. Five minutes after a connection was opened, the next call for that host closes it and opens another one -- whatever is still running on it. An `ssh_run` that went async (`exec_id`) or an SFTP transfer from `proxmox_upload_file` that crosses the five-minute mark gets its connection closed under it by any unrelated call to the same host.

There is also no lock around check / connect / store. Two concurrent calls to a host with no cached connection each open one; the second overwrites the first in the dict, and the first is never closed.

## Changes

- cache entries are a small `_CachedConnection` (`conn`, `created_at`, `last_used`, `active`)
- the TTL is idle time since last use, refreshed on every acquisition
- `_use_connection()` context manager pins the connection (`active += 1`) for the duration of the call; `exec_command`, the async-exec task and the three SFTP helpers go through it. A pinned connection is never expired for idleness
- one `asyncio.Lock` per host name around check / connect / store
- a closed connection is still detected and replaced, pinned or not
- `_get_connection` keeps its signature

## Known and left alone

- No maximum age: a connection in constant use lives until the server closes it. The old code had no cap beyond the TTL either; say if you want one.
- The lock is held during the connect, so a host that hangs on connect makes the other callers for *that host* wait for the connect timeout instead of each opening their own. Other hosts are not affected.
- `is_closed()` does not see a half-dead TCP connection. Same as before: the next command on it fails.
- Locks live in a module-level dict, like the cache. One event loop in production; the tests clear it in a fixture.

## Tests

998 passed, ruff clean, Python 3.12. New `tests/test_ssh_connection_cache.py`: recently used but old connection is reused, idle one is closed and replaced, expired-but-busy one is kept, two concurrent acquisitions give a single `connect`, closed one is replaced.

+"""SSH connection cache: idle expiry, in-use protection, one connect per host."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+from beaconmcp.ssh import client as ssh_client
+from beaconmcp.ssh.client import SSHClient
+
+
+class FakeConn:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.closed = False
+        self.close_calls = 0
+
+    def is_closed(self) -> bool:
+        return self.closed
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self.closed = True
+        self.close_calls += 1
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def harness(monkeypatch):
+    ssh_client._connection_cache.clear()
+    ssh_client._connection_locks.clear()
+    conns: list[FakeConn] = []
+
+    async def fake_connect(spec, policy):
+        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)  # yield so concurrent callers interleave
+        conn = FakeConn()
+        conns.append(conn)
+        return conn
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ssh_client, "_connect_to_host", fake_connect)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(ssh_client, "host_key_policy", lambda cfg, spec: None)
+    client = SSHClient.__new__(SSHClient)
+    client._config = None
+    monkeypatch.setattr(client, "resolve", lambda ident: SimpleNamespace(name="h"), raising=False)
+    yield client, conns
+    ssh_client._connection_cache.clear()
+    ssh_client._connection_locks.clear()
+
+
+def _entry(name: str = "h"):
+    return ssh_client._connection_cache[name]
+
+
+async def test_recently_used_old_connection_is_reused(harness) -> None:
+    client, conns = harness
+    first = await client._get_connection("h")
+    _entry().created_at -= 10 * ssh_client._CONNECTION_TTL  # created long ago
+    assert await client._get_connection("h") is first
+    assert len(conns) == 1 and not first.closed
+
+
+async def test_idle_connection_is_replaced_and_closed(harness) -> None:
+    client, conns = harness
+    first = await client._get_connection("h")
+    _entry().last_used -= ssh_client._CONNECTION_TTL + 1
+    second = await client._get_connection("h")
+    assert second is not first
+    assert first.closed and not second.closed
+    assert len(conns) == 2
+
+
+async def test_idle_connection_with_running_command_is_kept(harness) -> None:
+    client, conns = harness
+    async with client._use_connection("h") as first:
+        _entry().last_used -= ssh_client._CONNECTION_TTL + 1

+    assert await client._get_connection("h") is first

+

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(bmc): bind the ilo ssh tunnel to loopback

## Why

Found while re-reading `main` at 861748a after #67 and #70 landed. When a BMC device has a `jump_host`, `HPILOBackend._resolve_endpoint` opens the port-forward with an empty listen host (`src/beaconmcp/bmc/hp_ilo.py:72`). For asyncssh, `""` means every interface, so the iLO's HTTPS ends up reachable from the whole LAN on an ephemeral port of the BeaconMCP host for as long as the tunnel lives -- which is exactly what the jump host was there to prevent.

The client side already targets `127.0.0.1` (`_resolve_endpoint` returns `("127.0.0.1", port)` and `_call` hands that to `hpilo.Ilo`), so nothing depended on the wide bind.

## Changes

- listen on `127.0.0.1` instead of `""` in `HPILOBackend._resolve_endpoint`
- regression test on the address handed to `forward_local_port`

## Known and left alone

- The test checks the argument given to asyncssh, not a real socket bind.
- `forward_local_port` has a single call site in `src`, so there is no second tunnel to fix.
- Only setups with a `jump_host` on a BMC device are affected. Mine has no `bmc` block, so this is from reading the code, not from a live reproduction.

## Tests

994 passed, ruff clean, Python 3.12.

benchmarks.task_description: fix(discord): isolate per-message failures in the polled emit path ## What `_emit_polled_message` added the message id to the seen-set and then parsed and queued the message without a guard. Any exception after `seen.add` (a structurally malformed payload such as a non-dict `author`, or a `TradeSignal` that rejects a non-finite price) propagated to `_poll_loop`, which logged `Discord poll iteration failed`. The message id stayed in `seen`, so the poison message was skipped forever, and the rest of its page was not emitted for that poll. The parse/queue body moved to `_emit_parsed_message`; `_emit_polled_message` keeps the dedupe and the `seen.add` (so one poison message cannot block a channel) and wraps the call per message: - any exception is logged at **ERROR** as `Discord message dropped: emission failed` with `bot_name`, `service_id`, `channel_id`, `message_id`, `error` and `error_type`, so a dropped signal is visible in ops; - the poll continues with the next message of the page; - `asyncio.CancelledError` is re-raised, so shutdown is not swallowed. Fetch-side errors keep their existing behaviour: 401/403/429 still raise the dedicated Discord errors, so auth failure, per-channel skip and rate-limit backoff are unchanged. ## Why A single bad message must not cost the rest of its page, and it must not fail silently: the id stays in `seen` (a retry loop against a deterministic parse error would spin on every poll), while the ERROR log names the message so an operator can see which signal was dropped. ## Tests - New `TestIssue232PoisonMessage` (5 tests): ERROR log fields for a parser that raises, the rest of the page still queued and the cursor still advancing, a real malformed `author` row skipped instead of aborting the page, a repeated poison row not re-parsed, and `CancelledError` propagating through the guard. - All 5 fail on `origin/main` (verified by running them against the pre-fix module) and pass after the fix. - `tests/live_runner/test_discord_ingestion_gates.py` 205 passed, `test_discord_exit_and_levels_parsing.py` + `test_discord_price_tokens.py` 124 passed. - Full suite: `pytest -m "not slow" --ignore=tests/strategies -n 2` → 5945 passed, 13 skipped. - `PYTHON=$PY scripts/gate-tests.sh` → all 5 gate suites passed. - `ruff check` on both changed files: only the pre-existing `E501` at `discord_source.py:1540` on `main` (not touched here). ## Open decision None. The issue's proposal (per-message catch, ERROR with channel/message id, keep the id in `seen`, continue the page) is implemented as written. Closes #232 Step 5 Preview (Pi), T3 Code --- ## Summary by cubic Keeps one bad Discord message from silencing the rest of its poll page. Previously a message that failed to parse after its id was added to the seen-set aborted the whole poll iteration, logged a generic error, and was skipped forever; now the id stays in `seen` and the poll continues with the remaining messages. - Parse failures are logged at ERROR as `Discord message dropped: emission failed`, including bot name, channel id, message id, error, and error type. - A poison message is skipped exactly once and never retried, while the cursor still advances past it. - `asyncio.CancelledError` still propagates so shutdown is unaffected. - Fetch-side behavior (401/403/429 errors, rate limiting) is unchanged. - Adds regression tests for malformed `author` rows, non-finite prices, retry prevention, and cancellation, plus a note in `docs/signal_bots.md`. - Closes #232. Written for commit b9cf8b6d04730182449ee69bf0e902d78d64f46d. Summary will update on new commits.
